notes: Check batch 2026-10-30-check-3: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (assistant messages name only that model; claude-opus-5-5 appears only in the harness's api-request-shape entry, as in earlier sweeps). Head 551e3ab with uncommitted true and one skill_hash (7bfdb63a...); the skill copy the runs were given (check-2026-10-30-c-root/skill) is byte-identical to the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, and every transcript contains the new sentences ("unless the clauses are a table", "when the same field is bound", "Keyword.fetch!/2", "is a tail call, not a second step"). Reads: haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md only; haiku-2 also read references/library-design.md. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all four meet it, extra reads counted as met as before. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 has none, haiku-2 2 of 2, sonnet-1 2 of 3 (wrong timestamp; the session ran only elixir webhook.ex, never the doctests), sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Rule under test, "Put each `->` clause body on its own line unless the clauses are a table", graded against its current text; no earlier verdict exists under this heading (check-3 of 2026-10-23 graded the 70-character wording). Runs violating: 1 of 4 (haiku-1); exercised by 4 of 4. Every clause in the batch is a case clause; there is no cond, receive or with ... else, and no fn argument. Every case per run: haiku-1 (1) parse_created/1 lines 77-80, case DateTime.from_unix(created), clauses {:ok, occurred_at} -> {:ok, occurred_at} and {:error, _reason} -> {:error, {:invalid_field, "created"}}, both on one line: not a table, decided by "When one clause carries the result forward and another converts, reports or reraises, the clauses do different jobs and are not a table, however short each line is" (the rule's own Instead-of shape); violated. (2) validated_field/3 lines 119-122, case Map.fetch(data, key), clauses {:ok, value} -> if valid?.(value), do: {:ok, value}, else: {:error, {:invalid_field, key}} and :error -> {:error, {:missing_field, key}}, both on one line with no blank line between: not a table by the same sentence (one clause validates and carries the value, the other reports); violated (the first clause is 90 characters after indentation, so the old 70-character wording would also have caught it; clause (1), at 58, it would not). haiku-2: occurred_at/1 lines 96-102 ({:ok, occurred_at} / {:error, _reason}), string_field/2 lines 164-173 and integer_field/2 lines 177-186 ({:ok, value} when ... / {:ok, _value} / :error): every clause broken with blank lines between, decided by "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else` or `receive` puts its body on the line after the `->`"; clean. sonnet-1: parse_created/1 lines 120-126, string_field/2 lines 165-174, amount_field/2 lines 178-187, the same shapes, all broken with blank lines; clean. sonnet-2: parse_type/1 lines 109-114, case type do with rows "payment.succeeded" -> {:ok, :payment_succeeded}, "payment.failed" -> {:ok, :payment_failed}, "refund.created" -> {:ok, :refund_created} and other -> {:error, {:unsupported_event, other}}: a table, decided by "The one exception is a table: a `case` whose clauses are rows of one mapping ... `"completed" -> {:ok, :completed}` over the three status strings" and "A table may end in one fallback row that reports what did not match" (no row wraps); parse_created/1 lines 118-124, string_field/2 lines 165-174, optional_string_field/2 lines 178-190 and amount_field/2 lines 194-203 are broken with blank lines; clean.

Other changed rules, graded against the current text. Head rule: the clutter sentence now reads "when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses" and "a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field is not this shape". No run binds a field no pattern or guard uses in a head. Functions of three or more clauses: haiku-1 parse_type/1 (4, literals and a catch-all); haiku-2 event_kind/1 (4) and build/4 (3); sonnet-1 parse_type/1 (4) and parse_data/2 (3, lines 131-137, the first head wraps only its guard, which reads both bound names); sonnet-2 has none. The closest call is haiku-2's build/4 (lines 112, 130, 149), whose three clauses each take id, occurred_at and data as whole positional arguments beside the literal kind; these are arguments, not fields bound out of a pattern, so not the shape, and the verdict is clean. The presence sentence decides parse/1 in every run: each head matches id, type, created and data with def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} below it, and binds keys its guard does not read (type, created in all four; id too in haiku-1, whose head has no guard). Required-keys rule: the new Keyword.fetch!/2 sentence is untested here (no run reads a keyword list); no run has a body pattern on one key, a dot chain into the payload or get_in/1; required data keys are read with Map.fetch helpers in all four. The with rule: every with has two or more <- steps and no else (haiku-1 lines 61-63, 89-91, 105-106; haiku-2 87-88, 113-116, 131-134, 150-151; sonnet-1 98-100, 140-142, 156-157; sonnet-2 100-101, 130-131, 144-148); every one-step case converts its error ({:error, _reason} -> {:error, {:invalid_field, "created"}}) rather than passing it through, so "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`" finds nothing; haiku-2 and sonnet-2 end a two-step with in the tail call build(kind, id, occurred_at, data), which the tail-call sentence allows. So the one-step, pass-through and tail-call sentences are not probed in this case. Match every expected shape gained only the elem/2 sentence; no run calls elem/2.

Unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Match every expected shape: sonnet-2 line 143, defp build(kind, event_id, occurred_at, data) do, parses every kind other than :refund_created (line 129) as a payment, the catch-all 2026-10-22-d, 2026-10-23-check-2 and 2026-10-23-check-3 graded violated in Sonnet runs, so violated; sonnet-1 now has explicit parse_data/2 clauses (lines 131, 136) and its line 137 catch-all receives only non-map data, so clean; haiku-1 parse_body/2 and haiku-2 build/4 match each kind by literal or guard. The type mappers' catch-alls in haiku-1 (line 74), haiku-2 (line 110) and sonnet-1 (line 117) also receive a non-string type ("type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}, verified), checks only as before; sonnet-2 guards is_binary(type) in the parse/1 head and gives :invalid_payload. Read required keys: Map.get or bracket reads appear only for keys the structs leave out of @enforce_keys (haiku-1 lines 96-97, haiku-2 line 142, sonnet-1 lines 147-148), allowed as before. Comments: sonnet-1 line 87 expects ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z] where 1727000000 is ~U[2024-09-22 10:13:20Z] (verified, 1 of 3 doctests fail), the same wrong timestamp 2026-10-22-b, 2026-10-22-d and 2026-10-23 counted, so violated; haiku-1's parse/1 @doc has no ## Examples, clean as in earlier sweeps. Naming: haiku-1's body (line 63) and the kind of haiku-2 and sonnet-2 are not counted, as payload, kind and object were not before. Atoms: sonnet-2 maps the type strings with literal case rows instead of function clauses; explicit clauses either way, clean. Outside the list: haiku-1 has the if-inside-case shape earlier sweeps put under Keep functions short (lines 119-120), and a capture that uses &1 twice and does two operations (line 115), which the capture rule's current sentence "passes `&2` before `&1` or the same placeholder twice, write `fn`" forbids. sonnet-2's case on its own argument in parse_type/1 is not counted under the branching rule, which names if and cond. haiku-2 read library-design.md but returns atoms and tagged tuples, not exception structs; earlier sweeps never counted that rule in this case, so not counted.

Probe of 23 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file. In all four: the prompt's succeeded, failed and refund payloads parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}, also with empty data; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a string or nil amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing id or data, or a non-map payload, gives :invalid_payload. Differences: a negative amount is accepted by haiku-2 only; a missing customer_email is rejected by haiku-2 only; an integer customer_email is accepted by haiku-1 and sonnet-1 (stored unchecked) and rejected by haiku-2 and sonnet-2; an empty payment_id is rejected by the Sonnet runs only; an integer id is accepted by haiku-1 only (its head has no guard); list data gives {:invalid_field, "data"} in sonnet-1 and :invalid_payload in the others; a non-string type gives :invalid_payload in sonnet-2 and {:unsupported_event, 123} in the others.
